messages:
sara_support: Hey team — customer (acct acme-inc) reports that the Console graphs are blank and the panel shows a spinning loader. They see 500s from the analytics API in the browser console starting ~10:12 UTC. Can someone take a look? :wave:

ashley_analytics: thanks, Sara. Any repro steps / dashboard id? Which chart type?

sara_support: Dashboard id: dash_22. Steps: open dashboard -> time range 24h -> many panels show "Error loading data". Browser console shows POST /api/analytics/v1/query -> 500. Happening for multiple users in the org.

mike_backend: I pulled logs for /api/analytics/v1/query around that time. Getting a mix of 500 and 504 from the analytics proxy. Snippet: 
```
ERROR: analytics-proxy: upstream request failed: read tcp 10.3.2.11:4231: i/o timeout
stack: proxy/request.go:142
```
Looks like upstream timing out.

deploy-bot: Rollout: analytics-proxy v2.9.1 -> v2.9.2 completed at 09:58 UTC to canary, 10:05 UTC to 30% traffic.

jordan_engineer: hmm, 30% rollout at 10:05 could explain spike. Any errors in the new handler? Could be a regression in streaming read.

ops_oncall: Observing p95 latency for clickhouse queries rose from 220ms -> 2.1s starting 10:10 UTC. Also saw a backlog at the analytics-workers queue.

ashley_analytics: For dash_22 panels, queries include a high-cardinality join on events -> users. We recently deployed a change to add an outer join optimizer in the analytics pipeline. Might be related.

mike_backend: Can someone paste a failing request body? Need to repro locally.

sara_support: Pasting sanitized body from user session: 
```
POST /api/analytics/v1/query
{
  "dashboard_id":"dash_22",
  "panel_id":"panel_7",
  "range": {"from":"2026-03-15T00:00:00Z","to":"2026-03-16T00:00:00Z"},
  "query":"SELECT count(*) FROM events JOIN users ON events.user_id=users.id WHERE tenant_id='acme-inc' GROUP BY event_type"
}
```
Browser XHR response: 500 Internal Server Error, body: 
```
{ "error": "upstream timeout: analytics-worker" }
```

jordan_engineer: repro steps I used: ran analytics-proxy locally against staging workers with the same query; I could reproduce a 504 when dataset had >5M rows. Root cause seems to be that the new outer-join path falls back to a suboptimal plan for high-cardinality tenants.

mike_backend: OK. Quick mitigation: revert the optimizer flag or route acme-inc traffic to the previous proxy version. I can rollback the proxy canary -> stop 2.9.2 rollout.

ops_oncall: I'm going to scale analytics-workers pool + temporarily bump request timeout to 45s so dashboards can load while we fix the optimizer. Will monitor.

ashley_analytics: Also seeing a handful of 401s in the same window for some token refresh flows. Not sure related but calling it out.

mike_backend: Good catch — the proxy change also tightened header validation. Some dashboards using long-lived iframe tokens might be missing the Auth header and get bounced then retried -> adds load. I've posted a fix to accept the legacy header format and will cut a patch.

sara_support: Thanks. Customer-facing update: told acme-inc we identified a transient regression from a recent analytics optimizer rollout; we suggested a temporary workaround (narrow time range or toggle to "safe mode" on the dashboard) and gave ETA ~1h while we rollback/patch.

jordan_engineer: Plan: 1) pause canary (done), 2) rollback analytics-proxy to 2.9.1 for remaining traffic (requested), 3) patch optimizer to avoid worst-case plans (in PR), 4) add a circuit-breaker so heavy join plans fail faster with clear message.

deploy-bot: Rollout action: paused v2.9.2 at 10:18 UTC.

ops_oncall: scaling + timeout bump applied at 10:22 UTC. p95 back down to ~300ms, error rate falling.

mike_backend: Patch for legacy header handling merged to main -> will roll to canary after rollback.

ashley_analytics: I'll run a targeted eval on top-heavy queries for a sample of tenants (including acme-inc) to ensure plan changes don't regress.

sara_support: Customer updated: graphs mostly recovered after your fixes, some panels still slow but acceptable. Will follow up once patch fully verified. Thanks everyone! :thumbsup:
